Perfume rating 4.01 out of 5 with 4,891 votes

Dolce&Gabbana by Dolce&Gabbana is a Floral Aldehyde fragrance for women. Dolce&Gabbana was launched in 1992. Dolce&Gabbana was created by Jean-Pierre Mary and Martine Pallix. Top notes are Aldehydes, Basil, Citruses, Ivy, Mandarin Orange, Freesia and Bergamot; middle notes are Carnation, Marigold, Coriander, Orange Blossom, Lily, Jasmine, Bulgarian Rose and Lily-of-the-Valley; base notes are Sandalwood, Vanilla, Musk and Tonka Bean.

This classical, intensive, feminine aroma belongs to the group of aldehyde-floral fragrances. This is the first fragrance of Dolce & Gabanna. The composition is based on contrasts: sweet and bitter, feminine and masculine. The top notes are aromatic-citrusy and include mandarin, bergamot, basil and aldehydes – a rather strong opening. The heart is feminine floral created of jasmine, floral-spicy carnation, sweet orange blossom and lily. Silky sandalwood in the base is complemented with the sweet and balsamic notes of vanilla, Tonka and musk. This fragrance is recommended for evening wear and special occasions. It was created in 1992.

All Reviews By Date

Kitty9

This perfume embodies the quintessence of timeless glamour a fragrance that feels as if it were lifted straight from the golden age of Hollywood. It unfolds with an air of classic sophistication, elegant and luminous, as though wrapped in the aura of a modern-day fairy tale. The composition recalls the refined beauty of Chanel No. 5 intertwined with the distinctive charm of Vivienne Westwood, creating a scent that feels undeniably expensive and impeccably tasteful.
It glides across the skin with a smooth, velvety grace, never harsh, never cloying just an effortlessly chic presence that enhances one’s natural allure. This is the kind of fragrance that tells a story, that lingers in memory, that announces itself not with loudness but with cultivated confidence. A truly enchanting scent for those who appreciate luxury in its most elegant form.

massimilianoinquieto 11/12/25 02:51

Non mi ero mai interessato ai profumi di Dolce&Gabbana, lo avevo sentiti su altre persone negli anni 90 ma non li conoscevo di persona.
Recentemente ho trovato un vintage euroitalia di questo col tappo rosso e devo notare che facevano profumi molto originali.
Si, un po strano come odore, sviluppa lentamente partendo con uno strano effetto ruvido,compatto,non ricorda niente di gia sentito,stranamente verde,un po pungente,decisamente diverso dai profumi attuali.
Non ha effetti liquorosi,non ha effetti frutta pllasticosa, non sa di roba da mangiare tipo vaniglie e cioccolato, o peggio, praline e per questo mi piace.
Sento che il cuore arriva lentamente e scalda la fragranza, rilassa il bouquet nevrotico della partenza ed esala note di comodità,confortevoli.
Più passa il tempo e più il profumo diventa buono,liscio, vellutato e caldo. Un floreale aldeidico su muschi morbidi,il cuore trabocca di fiori e c'è anche qualcosa di piccante.
Non avendolo mai usato prima, non mi ricorda nulla,ma leggo che è una fragranza molto amata quindi deduco che sia stata usata da molta gente.
L'ho indossato oggi ed è stata una meraviglia.

fleurdeme 09/30/25 17:58

I received a small splash bottle of YSL Libre last year and at once disliked it and secretly kind of didn’t mind it for occasional private wear. Why? It reminded me of a D&G red cap splash bottle I had in the late 90s. In fact, I was certain they shared the same dna, even the now commonplace (would pedestrian go too far?) modern gourmand-friendly, vanillic base.

So convinced was I that I purchased a travel spray of the D&G. Well I was oh so wrong! Even in the modern formulation D&G feels special. It’s aromatic, spicy, warm and comforting—yet alluring, elegant. But not commonplace. Maybe after so many years of drowning in patisserie accords, and as many people have noted, in the absence of the once omnipresent cigarette aromas, this just smells damn good to me.

Longevity wowwwwww it’s been going over 12 hours today! Loving this. It’s not yet time to worry about to FB or not to FB (and current or vintage? etc.). For now I will enjoy this perfume. It’s not the time capsule that I expected (that for whatever reason Libre is—Xina and Britney and low rise jeans and Candie’s), it strikes me as unexpectedly timeless. Or maybe it’s just an antidote to the gourmand crisis. Beautiful!

EllieJP 08/30/25 03:49

I have Italian-made bottles. Around 1992, during Japan’s bubble economy, these perfumes were widely available, so they’re relatively easy to find here！

They have a rare scent that brings back memories of the 1990s. On my skin, the aldehydes lingered longer than expected, revealing the floral notes not in an hour, but after about three hours. Honestly, I was surprised by that initial sparkling “bang” of fragrance. I recommend it when you want to immerse yourself in the 1990s vibe. I happen to have quite a few, so I’m planning to part with two Italian-made bottles.

*Telling Italian-made bottles apart is quite simple. The red cap is semi-transparent, not completely clear, and if you look closely, the bottom of the bottle forms a beautiful arch. Bottles made outside Italy do not have this elegant arched bottom. It’s impressive how much attention to detail goes into these subtle features.

LadyIva 10/22/24 08:52

This perfume was launched more than thirty years ago. Back then, it was quite normal for designer houses to create floral-aldehydic fragrances aimed at young girls. I was a dumb little high schooler then, and my small fragrance collection consisted of Yves Rocher Magnolia, CK One, some white musks, and such; my first 'serious' perfume was Givenchy Amarige. Nowadays, when I smell Amarige, I can't believe that I used to wear that as a teenager, because it's so floral and strong - but such were trends at that time. Some of my friends wore Dolce & Gabanna, but I never bought it because I thought that it was too similar to Amarige (and Cabotine).
Fast forward 30 years, and Dolce & Gabanna still smells like Amarige - I mean, they are far from clones, but they do belong to the same late 1980s - early 1990s trend of very pungent aldehydic florals. D&G contains many floral notes that were in vogue at that time, such as carnation, marigold, lily, and whatnot; yet, it is less heady than Amarige, thanks to herbal-aromatic notes in the opening. After a while, D&G becomes very soapy, courtesy of prominent aldehydes which overpower all the other notes. All in all, this fragrance is a remnant of its era; as such, it carries a certain nostalgic appeal to us who are old enough to remember the early 1990s - but I would never wear it today.

The perfume is blended very well and quite honestly, outside of the aldehydes, it's not easy to detect individual notes. There is a correlation with men's cologne, probably due to the sandalwood, basil, and coriander-but it still reads feminine, to me. It's a power scent to me-I see a boss bitch wearing this. Definitely could be a signature scent as well. I'm glad D&G is still making this and I hope they never stop. I feel like it's their Chanel #5 but for Gen X.

This can still be purchased directly from the D&G website. Also, wait at least 5 minutes before sniffing as it's intense/sharp until it dries, but once it dries, you get the full beauty of this scent.

I would consider this to be one of my classiest scents next to Chanel 5 L'Eau, Rouge Malachite, Coco Noir, Elie Saab, Santal Royal, Good Girl, Gone Bad (the dumbest name for an elegant white floral).

Similar to Chanel No 5 EDT, but cheaper and easier to wear.

No 5 has a sharp, acerbic edge which belongs in an era when it was acceptable for a feminine fragrance to choke everyone out and make their eyes water.

This is a softer, more modern approach to the same idea, albeit with almost as heroic and challenging a blast of aldehydes in the opening. The difference is the abundance of florals and citrus which accompany the abrasive chemical side. Everything is discernable here, and unilike no 5 I don't wince at the OTT scratchiness.

Needless to say I prefer this, and so does my wallet.

Update:
Now my bottle has had a few days to macerate, the perfume has blossomed. Instead of BAM ALDEHYDES IN YO FACE, it's a less histrionic, smoother mix of sparkle, citrus and florals, with a very dainty bed of patchouli carrying it.
FYI I have the new formulation and it's great. I'm not familiar with the old, and I don't see the point of bleating on about the differences and/or the fact it's lost...this phenomena is part and parcel of perfumery, suck it up.

As a perfume lover I was aware of this juice being the stuff of perfume legend, and the discontinuation was much lamented by the perfume community. The current Pour Femme with the small purple cap is an abomination in my opinion, a marshmallow, hairspray mess that actually makes me gag.
I bought a Euroitalia miniature on eBay but it had turned, although I could still smell some of the beauty of this and was determined to try a fresh or unspoiled bottle. I’ve managed to get hold of a Beaute Prestige Eau De Toilette bottle, made in France, from FragranceX (so definitely genuine). It arrived today, and I’ve not been this excited about a perfume arriving since I managed to snag a bottle of Versace Blonde. My word, this is stunning!
I can see the resemblance to Chanel No 5, sure there are aldehydes in here but they are creamy and well blended as opposed to the punchy, fresh air blast you get from no.5 (and which I love about no.5). If this had smelt like no.5 I would have been disappointed as I have that perfume and adore it and don’t need a dupe. There is a warmth in this perfume that no.5 doesn’t have. This definitely has the richness of no.5 though.
This smells like laundry drying in the sun in a hot country, as described by some others on here and I think it will work well in all seasons, even the hottest, where it will bloom on the skin. It’s like a really beautiful body lotion. I can’t pick out any particular notes and definitely not the coriander which I struggle with as a note.it is definitely aromatic as opposed to floral.
It reminds me a little of Joop and Gabriela sabatini’s perfume, although it is not a dupe of any of these. It smells timeless, classic and not dated in anyway.
The current formulation doesn’t seem to be as beast mode as original versions of the scent but nothing is beast mode nowadays with all these blasted reformulations, except a good oud perfume, Montale, La Vie est Belle or Baccarat. As @simplecreative has said, there’s nothing else out there that smells like this, so the lack of sillage and longevity is a compromise I am prepared to make to have this beautiful fragrance in my life.
Why on earth did D&G discontinue/severely scale down the production of this one? It’s signature material, and I, along with countless others would happy buy this on repeat for the rest of my days!

LivingForPerfumeFrenchie 12/23/22 14:13

The original version ( bright red cap ) is about as masterful as they come. It smells like royalty. If you put this on you smell like you own a palace, not even kidding!

So strong, it lasts days, on the skin and on the clothes ( even after washing !) Amazing projection ( room filling, more so house filling even ) and lasts for ages.

It has something official and serious to it, an elegance of royal stature. It has so much renaissance to it, so much beauty, like the Michelangelo ceilings.

Citrusy and a bit sharp on aldehydes at the top, It develops into beautiful flowers with aldehydes softer in the background over time. It leaves room for beautiful flowers and a soft hint of vanilla. You get the musk straight away, I smell it seconds after spraying. It's a beautiful round musk, not too dry.

It's not grandma soapy and sharp like Ungaro Diva at all. It's not the same ball park. I feel like Diva is just all a ton of flowers, powder and soap being thrown at you with sharp aldehydes for a very very long time. I only like the dry down after hours with Diva.

DG I enjoy instantly, even if the first 5 minutes are quite intense because it's an absolute beast.

Yes the aldehydes are a bit sharp / screechy at the start with D&G PF, but it gets balanced out very fast and the mid and base just continue non stop glory. It glides. It's not first : boom ! and then gone. There is a whole 48 hour journey with this one. The power is like magic, it never dies, there is a consistency to it, whilst also allowing different notes to shine as you go through your 48 hour journey with this royal fragrance.

This perfume just smells like the Queen. No other way to put it. It smells like old money and a kingdom and several palaces in Europe. It elevates anyone who wears it, like a crown. It makes you want to buy golden cutlery, expensive paintings and antique jewellery of high value. It makes you want to go to high luxury hotels, and have front seat at the races next to the Queen.

Not for the faint hearted. This is for people who want a powerful royal elegant bomb. This perfume is the epicentre of sophistication and royal status.

A nice perfume friend here gave me a vintage decant of this iconic fragrance. I wonder if the new reformulation is as good as this is. This reminds me a bit of Ysatis by Givenchy only in that it is a powerhouse aldehydic floral from the 20th century. A century I still miss very much. Ysatis has the greenness of galbanum and creamy white florals that are amped up w/ powerful aldehydes. D&G has the fresh spicy greenness of basil but instead of white florals it is carnation that is the star of the show w/ those powerful aldehydes. This is not a sweet perfume, and you probably have to be a certain age to appreciate this perfume, I am 52 and I enjoy this type of scent profile. I can see why D&G is compared to #5 but for some reason #5 or any Chanel for that matter never works for me. I don't need a full bottle of this, my decant will be enough since my favorite aldehydes (when I crave them) are White Diamonds, Joy, 1000, Un Amour, Enjoy, Aprege, L'Heure Attendue (Heritage Collection Jean Patou) Priscilla Presley's Roses and More and the new 21st century type Fox in a Flowerbed. But this is very enjoyable when applied w/ a light hand (a little goes a very long way) Carnation is powerful even w/out aldehydes. You have to really enjoy both those notes to enjoy this perfume. Soapy, fresh like a very clean white shirt, fresh spicy floral of yesteryear.

Edit: 11/30/22 Damn wearing this again now and I think I need a full bottle. This perfume really seduces you. At first, I thought I have enough aldehydic florals I don't need another one, but I was wrong. D&G is really special and what makes it special is the carnation spiciness which is a real standout since most aldehydic florals are based on white florals. I will be ordering this right way. I bought this immediately after reading through the countless reviews of this scent and scent memories, and I wasn't deterred that I'd be unable to buy the original Italian formulation. I was lucky enough to get the red cap very quickly in the mail which I tore open as soon as I received it.

I didn't really understand it and I couldn't have. It's the kind of scent you just have to smell for yourself. This is probably THE most game-changing scent I have ever got my hands on. I'm now scared it's going to be unavailable at some point and am trying to pace myself in acquiring more bottles.

It's kind of indescribable to me, and the only thing I can really convey is the soapy-aldehydic part of it--but there really is alot more going on here. I just can't describe it because I am not literate enough in notes to really discern them. One of the reviews said it smelled like a bank when you first walk in and I completely agree - it's bizarre, but it does. Like when you first walk in to a bank that is highly air conditioned and the smell of money just hits you in the nose. For this reason I wear this mostly to work; it's definitely not a casual scent, really, in any way. In an off-work setting, I can see someone possibly wearing this to an outdoor event, as the sillage is so great on this it would be noticeable even with other smells and in a light breeze. I may try to wear it to dinner at some point but for now it's a power suit accompaniment. Not sure I'd wear it in the heat as it could be suffocating.

It lasts all day and then some and to me it never really changes after that first half hour or so. My 7 year old got her hands on it and sprayed it all over herself a couple weeks ago, and while it definitely seemed out of place on her, the projection was stable into the evening, and consistently wafted gently behind her as she moved.

The opinions of this scent aren't as hot and cold as I expected they would be, with most people on the "love" side, but I can actually see this one being a love it/hate it kind of smell. It is not safe blind buy. Although it was a huge win for me, I took to it only after my husband sprayed it on his wrist and I had a chance to smell it from a distance. I think was a bit confusing for me when I smelled it on myself. Somehow, the distance made it easier to absorb and fully appreciate the notes; maybe it was because I was perceiving it as masculine on him vs trying to align it with whatever original expectations I had before opening the box. Once I realized how much I loved it on him, I asked him to wear it a few times more, and then eventually took it over again for myself. Not sure if there is any place to get a decant of this, but even if you wind up with a whole bottle and don't like it, I'm sure you won't have a hard time finding someone who will take it off of your hands given the extreme love for this.

For me, this fragrance is the epitome of glamour. I want to share with you the story of my parents’ friend Brigitte…

Brigitte is French. She smokes long cigarettes, drinks wine and hosts fabulous but laid back parties. She has olive skin, short dyed caramel hair and wears gold jewellery. She’s unashamedly herself. She has a sultry low voice and laughs loudly and unreservedly. She’s fiercely loyal. Nails always done. She rides motorbikes. She wears D&G red cap.

I know this doesn’t tell you much about the fragrance itself but all the notes are listed here anyway. I remember it as very soapy but that description really doesn’t do it justice. It’s soapy in a refined, pure and very expensive way.

You might expect someone like Brigitte to wear a smoky, oriental scent. But she didn’t need it. She smoked Marlboros and wore high quality leather. She was also a mother and wife who was always well turned out and impeccably stylish. This scent just suited her perfectly.

Brigitte moved back to France, and I haven’t seen her in years. But she left an impression on me. She became my reference point for glamour at such a young age, before I even knew what glamour was.

In sum, this fragrance is classy, sophisticated and timeless - much like Brigitte!!

From a Man's Perspective, One of the Ultimate Womens' Frags.
(Based on the 90s original)

Intimidate your secret lovers.
Intimidate the man in your life.
Intimidate that woman you always wanted to have sex with & finally did.
Intimidate your workmates.
Why not intimidate your mother-in-law too.

This was the 1st frag that D & G launched after their clothing design broke internationally.

I remember at the time, their words to effect were......they wanted to create a perfume in the iconic style of luxe, riche women's perfumes....... & they nailed it!

When asked by reporters if they intended expanding into other lines, they replied to effect if they 'ever did' cosmetics, they would do just a 'great' red lipstick & a luxury compact.

Well that's the image '& smell' I get as a man reviewing this juice.

A beautiful woman....not a girl, popping out her luxury compact & touching up her lipstick.

Aldehydic, acid, powder, Guerlainade-like treatment of florals, "nose-feel tickle" but not in an irritating way. Dry down to musk & the 'presence' of skin.

And that packaging!

That tall rectangular bottle & the block-across-the-top red cap! Understated arrogance at it's most potent.

The concept of this sorting the women-the-women-from-the-girls is irrelevant here, because any 'girl' wouldn't survive 10minutes in the same room with this stuff.

I believe fragrance can be many things on many occasions. And one of those things is a safe space, where doing no harm to self & others: Every man can be a selfish arrogant bastard. And every woman can be an entitled spoilt bitch.

This is definitely "that space" for latter of the above.

Sensuality weaponized!
I'm standing back & keeping well out of the way!

This eau de toilette has more potency than most of my eau de parfum concentrations. Impressive.

Dolce & Gabbana, for me, is the ultimate old Hollywood bombshell fragrance. Immaculate, classic silver screen beauty. The soft voluptuousness of Marilyn Monroe. Rita Hayworth smouldering in Gilda. Ava Gardner lounging in the most sensual silk satin gown. So sexy. So rich & creamy, with some elements of freshness that never take centre stage or become annoying. Such an unusual combination of notes not often (ever?) seen in recent mainstream perfumery… & that always catches my interest. Even though it was love at first sniff for me, it’s a complex scent that takes you on a journey. Some have described it as linear, but that’s not my experience at all. Objectively, I can see why men would love this, both on themselves & others, as it straddles that line perfectly between what people generally think of as feminine / masculine. Having said that, I do not personally perceive this as "masculine". It's a solid film noir femme fatale in my mind. A refined, adult woman. Not a girl. A strong personality. This is a person who knows themselves & never indulges others immaturity. Perfumes like this just aren’t made anymore, except in the niche world. I would say it's not difficult to wear at all, but it has to be for you.

echurch1979 04/22/21 00:49

Dolce & Gabbana is one on a short list, that blew my mind wide open to a future in perfume adoration and analysis. Almost thirty years have passed since that first spray and enchanted eye roll. Despite a necessary reformulation to achieve code standards, and subsequently somewhat deflated, D & G still sings radiantly. Shortly after I summoned the courage to drain the bank of a considerable sum of money, I repurchased this beauty, lovingly referred to as the "Red Top". I reviewed my previous assessment of components listed, and was shocked at how close the new formulation was, considering I based the old on a memory. That is the bewitching nature of this, that one can recall a memory from almost thirty years ago with such accuracy. It is also a testament to the perfumers involved with its re-release. I carefully compared notes, giving pause to sandalwood, lily of the valley, and musk, who have been synthesized for some time now. I still love the coldness of herbal notes and citruses, juxtaposed with the spicy warmness of woods, musk and vanilla. The contrast also continues with the sheer brightness of freesia, jasmine and ivy, against sweet and spicy marigold, carnation, and rose. Up until tonight, I regarded this perfume as a sweater-weather treat, an intrinsic heat captured through the glow of honey peaking past glass. I never even thought of this creation as being aldehydic dominant, let alone composed of so much of that olfactory albatross. Where have I been? As I smell the blotter again and again, I can't help wondering why I didn't detect that before. Plain to see now, I guess that's what they say about hindsight. One thing is for certain in my mind, and that is how dazzling she still is after all this time - how wonderfully she's aged. And how content am I, after finally being reunited with an old friend!

The perfume that started my obsession with perfumery.
My love affair with this gem goes back all the way to the late 90s when I was merely 8 or 9 at the time. My family had just started seeing this rich, sophisticated and refined-tasted woman who lived abroad and had a son who owned a perfume store in London. She always smelled of D&G Red. She was a smoker so the cigarette smoke dampened the soapiness aspects of the fragrance and enhanced the magical ambery/floral/vanillic/musky base. Her entire house smelled like Red when we went to visit her. When she came to visit us, I could smell her perfume trail all the way to the second floor. She also had an arts and crafts hobby where she’d make really pretty gift baskets and gift them to her friends. One day, she sent my mom a gift bag and sprayed the inside of the bag with Red. It smelled like heaven to me. I remember clutching the paper bag wherever I went and taking whiffs of it every now and then to enjoy its magic. Sadly, I never got to know what perfume she actually wore and we have largely lost touch with the woman. Many years later in my early to mid 20s I’d spend hours on this site trying to find this elusive sent that captivated me as a child. This perfume (along with By Man by D&G which was gifted to me by the same lady) is responsible for my interest in perfumery. Many hours, and a dozen of decants later, my sister actually remembered what the perfume bottle looked like and she told me it was a dolce&gabbana bottle with a red cap. Purchased the 4ml mini sample off ebay first, and it barely resembled how I remember it smelling like. It was just too soapy and clean. Not at all the dark, musky, strong woman scent I remember it to be. Fast forward a couple of years later and I recently found a used, reasonably-priced bottle with a 2001 batch code being sold on eBay. Maybe it’s the age, but this particular bottle has the gorgeous base I came to enjoy from the scent. The aldehydic soapiness is still there, but It’s dialed down a bit compared to the 4ml mini bottle. I also found that the trick is to smell the scent cloud rather than stick your nose towards on your wrist to get whiffs of that base.

Beautiful scent with amazing longevity. The vibe of the scent is most suitable for women with an edge imo. Feminine in style but has an Animus quality to her. Think Catherine Tramell in Basic Instinct or Samantha Jones in Sex And The City. 10/10 for the dry-down. So happy I finally found it.

Mel_Nocturnum 09/26/20 09:49

The famous Red Cap!
Reading reviews, and people commenting on its bright aldehydes, I was curious but never really looked for it.
But a month ago I found on a French site a sealed bottle of the original, with a 1991 batch code.
Price was good, I love aldehydes and Italian bombastic-ness so I jumped right in.

Now, I have to say that while I love it, I don’t find it the aldehyde bomb it’s made to be.
Maybe I’m so used to them in vintage jewels like Calèche, Rive Gauche or Chanel N°5, that they strike me here as effervescent bubbles ready to pop.
The jewel here is the creamy, languorous drydown that follows the spicy floral heart.
Yeah, the aldehydes brighten and lift, giving volume and texture to the other notes. But what shines is a spicy carnation, big as a 1980’s Teatro Alla Scala, softened by jasmine and lily, and made even more fiery by a wonderful coriander (why isn’t coriander used more often??) note and a pinch of basil.

The notes dance with each other, and it’s hard to pinpoint them. There’s artistry in the blending, and as a whole I can see why it’s so hot tempered. It’s exotic, erotic, sensual and big, just like perfumes used to be.
The florals take a more oriental turn as the drydown approaches, and the vanilla/sandalwood combo reminds me slightly of what the future Addict would employ in its own basenotes.

I love it. And I can see why everyone misses it. There’s a slight hairspray feel to it which I love, but more of a boudoir scent, not richly coiffed hair. The woman (or man) using it, is ready to take the world by the balls and make it their own.
If only D&G had stayed on that route...of real perfume that is.
Sillage/longevity; from Rome to Milan, all the way through the Italian countryside.

Absolutely beautiful!
I'm not a vintage perfume person, as a general rule I like scents from the 90s and newer. This is from the 90s, but has some notes that were at their most popular long before that, namely aldehydes and carnation. Out of all the currently unpopular notes, these are the two that I would love to smell more often in modern perfumery, but I was still a little wary because don't always love them in older scents. Unnecessarily so! Together with the warm base of this fragrance, they smell timeless and not dated at all.

D&G opens with a burst of soapy, bubbly, fizzy aldehydes. After many reviews about this being such a sexy, dramatic diva perfume I was quite surprised by how clean it is. There is a sensual warmth beneath the cleanliness, but nothing animalic or otherwise wild. Just a lot of soothing sandalwood, a hint of vanilla that intensifies in the late drydown, a floral bouquet that mainly consists of carnations, and some aromatic, spicy notes which smell like more than just coriander and basil to me.
So I really think that this can easily be worn daily as a casually chic and elegant scent. I guess it all depends on your own style and perspective, but if you wear red lipstick in your day-to-day life, this won't feel out of place either.
The reviewers who mentioned fluffy clean towels are spot on. I'm sure towels don't really smell different from other fresh laundry, but this fragrance is the texture and feel of a fresh warm towel translated into scent.

My sample is from P&G prestige. I have never tried any older versions, nor do I care to hunt them down as I already love this one.
It's kind of confusing, some say this is discontinued, some say this is back in stores. Despite my version being made in Germany, which is where I live, it has been almost impossible to find here for years. DieT CroaK 06/26/20 10:39

Ooooh! This is a nice one! Let me just say that I fell down the rabbit hole trying to find THE soapy fragrance. D&G Red Cap was suggested. People described it as fresh, fizzy and spicy. I don’t know why but the fizzy drew me in. I went on Ebay and found a 3.4oz bottle of this baby for about $70 which isn’t bad considering it’s nearly impossible to find in U.S. stores. Now, I know that people are claiming that the German formulation (which I have) pales in comparison to the Euroitalia version. From the batch number, I was able to tell that mine was manufactured in September 2012. From what I understand, all perfumes were watered down after 2012 in order to comply with IFRA so I am sure that the Italian versions are stronger. Does that mean that they are superior? Maybe. German formulations are manufactured by Procter & Gamble Prestige Beaute. The newest formulations are coming from France still under P&G so if you’re interested in Red Cap, do your homework and figure out which formulation is going to be best for you. Also, beware of fakes because they are aplenty.

Anyway, I had D&G Light Blue back when it first came out. Funny side note: my best friend set me up on a blind date with a guy and I wore Light Blue that night. I caught a whiff of him mid-date and asked him what he was wearing. It was Light Blue for men. Cute, right?!? We wore the same fragrance on the first date! This has to be fate 🥰 I wish I could wrap up the story by saying we got married and had a Light Blue bottle cake at our wedding but no...He ended up breaking my heart and wasting my time. Certified F boy. That’s probably why I ended up hating that particular fragrance. I chucked my 75% full bottle into the garbage after we broke up. Yeah, I know. Dramatic. Not only that but everywhere I went, I was bound to smell it on someone. I just got sick of it. So, I am already biased against D&G lol. This is like the Matrix, Blue cap will sedate you and blend you with the masses. Red invigorates you and sets you apart from the usual. I really should have gone red! But I feel like nobody talks about Red because Blue is always shoved into the undeserved limelight. I had to do some real digging to even find a mention of this fragrance and how beautiful it is. The YouTube review from Ouch110 was what really sold me. Also, he delves deeply into the reformulation history and breaks down the differences in each one. Okay, Ouch. I will give D&G another chance...

The initial spray of this is SPICY. For a minute, I was like, “Wait! Did I buy the wrong bottle?!?!” The dry down is where this fragrance really takes off. I get that fizzy, sparkly, airy sensation. It truly does smell like warm laundry fresh from the dryer. The basil in this gives it that unexpected bitter, spicy twist that sets it apart from your standard fresh and clean scent. I don’t feel like it’s overpowering which you think it would be from the first spray. It’s soft and bold at the same time. Feminine with a hint of a freshly washed baby. I’m not a girl, not yet a woman type of vibe (I hear Britney Spears is actually a fan of this scent). I really love this! The staying power is pretty good. It’s still detectable after the 5 hour mark but definitely gone by morning. That must be why people prefer the Euroitalia version. BUT... it’s still great! I totally get why people keep coming back to this fragrance after almost 30 years. Sure, it does smell “classic”, aldehydes do that. But there’s something sweet and innocent intertwined at the heart of it also.
Red, you’re the real showstopper here 🤩. I don’t care what anyone says about your Cool Watery, screechy, overhyped Blue little sister. I live in Chicago and as diverse as we are, I can tell you that I have yet to smell anything quite unique as Red Cap on someone. I smell a lot of Gucci, Mugler, Lancome, Juicy Couture, Bath and Body Works and yes, still to this day, Blue Cap. I actually smelled Blue Cap on a woman at work the other day and I have to admit that it smelled pretty good on her. But overall, Red Cap is much cooler and exotic. I feel like it’s finally gaining the hype and recognition it’s always deserved.

Update: As of February 2022, D&G has decided to split from Shiseido and is now planning on revamping/restoring all fragrances back to the Euroitalia quality. Does this mean we can expect to see a revival of Red Cap in its original glory?!? Stay tuned.

One of my absolute favorite things about perfume is its ability to challenge our perceptions of what we *think* we like or don't like from moment to moment and year to year as our tastes evolve. This just happened with me today, with my early 90's bottle of Dolce and Gabbana. It's exactly how I always remember it, but while I used to quite loathe it I now love it...I suddenly just *get* what it's going for. The glorious, airy, powdery aldehydes, the sweet, herbaceous basil, the green and tender ivy, warm sandalwood and softly spicy carnation are all the same, but my perception about them is just completely different ...wonderfully, beautifully so.

I agree with Coffee_Girl in that I don't find it so utterly sexy, except maybe in a "girl next door" way. I don't get anything sharp or masculine, nothing "dirty" or carnal, and it's not really a powerhouse to my nose, either. It's soft, clean, cozy and warm, and quite feminine ...rather lush, but serene. It's potent for sure, but that can be tempered by how much you apply ...though frankly, I feel like applying a *lot*, lol. I really want to just lavish it on and celebrate the fact that I don't have to go on the hunt for a vintage bottle!

This magical experience is why I don't just collect perfumes but truly love them, and have a very difficult time parting with any of them, even when we don't initially get along so well. I'm still waiting and hoping to love Shalimar ...some day.

mschnabel666 06/26/18 07:29

I'm so late to this party, but I got two bottles of the vintage "Made in Italy" off ebay for great prices (both sealed in velvet boxes)! One is probably a 1995 bottle with "Fl Oz" on the box, and less ingredients printed on the box. The 2nd bottle has "FL OZ" on the box, more ingredients. The 1995 is stronger, but not by much. Also could be the age. The 1995 had a bit of evaporation which can make a scent thicker and more syrupy.

This was a blind buy for me, but I adore vintage scents and I love aldehydes. Truthfully tho, I had no clue what to expect.

Both bottles had some evaporation and/or leakage so I could SMELL them without spraying. And that is an odd smell. And not a good smell. It's very cheap disinfectant/public bathroom cleaner. Strong and chemical like COMET powder cleaner. Who would want to smell like this? It's soooooo harsh, cloying and SOAPY?! WTF?! I like soapy but this is EXTREME!

But... hey now... This must be misted on skin. Not applied in heavy layers on the same skin area. Not on fabric. When worn on fabric or heavily sprayed on the same skin area-- it stays linear and cloying-- that harsh chemical soap. But misted right on skin-- MAGIC! Let it melt into you and radiate with movement/body heat/wind.

My skin is oily by genetics, but DRY and pale by climate. And it was a sunny breezy summer Michigan day. Not hot, but not cold. A hoodie day!

I did about 5 sprays on my bare chest/arms and then dressed. At first I only got the soap and felt like my bottle could be fake/turned because it wasn't NUCLEAR yet.

In the clean sharp aldehydes are POPS of scent. It's very layered and changes. I didn't really get an open/middle/base but more POPs of scent. While I washed dishes I got citrus and sweet. My skin radiated a SWEET creamy powdery smell. My shirt gave off the soap/aldehydes. I got some animalic musk too.

Sweet and bitter indeed! Bitter sharp soap, but some kind of creamy WARM sweet powder. Citrus thrown in. The herbs make the aldehydes very "nose hair burning", and the spices are just hints here and there.

What a strange and wonderful perfume! You can smell the quality because it needs SKIN and chemistry and body heat to change and develop. This only smells dated in the fact that you must have smelled it somewhere in the last 25 years. This smells like a mature woman because those women have been wearing it as a signature for 25 years. And of course, it's nothing like today's perfume. You also never smell this kind of quality anymore, except maybe for Mugler.

I find this nothing like L'Heure Bleue or Chanel No. 5. This isn't overly WOMANLY, but it's unique. Are you clean? Or skanky? Soapy or sweet? It doesn't really develop on me to be one gender or the other. I do feel however, that this perfume wears ME-- it's not 100% my style/vibe, nor do I feel it's a good match for my chemistry. But I still like it. It's fun to wear!

Not much shirt scent left the next morning which is OK by me. Sometimes a perfume lasts thru a washing, or clings to a sweater/jacket you may not wash every time you wear. I like a strong perfume- believe that- but I also like a fresh start after I wash something. I have over 300 perfumes... haha.... I certainly don't want to wear the same one every time I wear a certain outfit. ;) (I'm looking at you Dior Addict and Alien Essence Absolue)

The 2nd day of a tissue test-- clean/soap/powder but musky SKIN. It smells soapy still but this warm powdery musk. Nice. Very light 2nd day tissue smell. Overall, yes- this is potent, but when worn correctly- it can be perfect! It also doesn't have to be cloying or offensive. I find Classique EDT to be WAY more out there/strong/soapy/powder on steroids. (In the spirit of the 90s, I wore Classique EDP to work today, haha)

samantham-123 06/18/18 03:22

I can't believe how quickly i fell in love with this!

How can such a masculine combination of notes create something so unbelievably feminine?!

This is really lovely.

I originally wanted Sicily because the notes and reviews made it sound so amazing, but i ordered a 2ml sample and yes, it was very nice but i just couldn't justify paying through the nose for it. So i thought ide give red cap a try, but given that it seems so polarizing and many have warned against blind buying it, i again got a 2ml sample, and from the first sniff i was in love. Clearly, this is the D&G for me.

I have actually been wanting a to finally get a bottle of chanel no5 because i have always adored it but didnt think i was ready to wear it, now i feel like im finally at the point in my life were i am ready for a strong, classic feminine fragrance, but i actually gave the old chanel a pass and went online and ordered a bottle of D&G redcap, im assuming its the re released version as it was reasonably priced, but even the pre reformulated version is better priced than chanel so im glad i like this one lol.

Onto the scent itself,
I was weary, anticipating a very overwhelming dusty soapy powderbomb. But what I got was a beautiful sparkly aldehyde and citrus opening that soon became a warm sweet floral boquet that i cant really define into individual notes as it was so incredibly smooth. I could actually pick up the basil but it was just enough to give it a slight green sweetness; i have never smelled basil in perfume before but it was suprisingly light and fresh. Yes there was a little soapyness to it but not as much as i was expecting going by other reviews, to me its more powdery, but in a ...i cant really explain; like, an ulta high end make up powder, and sort of creamy at the same time. I dunno, its hard to explain so I'll just emphasize that it is truly beautiful.
Like Sicily, dolce and Gabbana have managed to make a classic smelling fragrance for modern women. It has all the beauty and unique class of a vintage scent, but with a light, youthful freshness. I despise the term " granny smell", i think anyone should wear what they love regardless of age.

The final drydown has lasted about 5 hours and still going strong, which is now a warm, slightly smoky, slightly sweet musky skinscent, i did spray very lightly so i think if i went heavier on this ide get a good day out of it at least.

Body chemistry must be of great importance when wearing this, as some have said its a soapy mess, other reveiwers have said it gives them headaches and then others just can't get enough of it. Im with the latter; i rarely react to a fragrance the way i did with this, from the first sniff i couldnt stop breathing it in and thinking " omg thats goooood!"

Im glad i gave it a chance because the notes listed are not what i would usually go for, but sometimes you just surprise yourself.
I dont quite understand the marketing with the new pour femme; d&g saying that theyve grown a lot since the 90's and its not so much a new fragrance, as it is fine tuning...
theyre two different scents, straight out opposites. And while i do like the new one ( i didnt at first but that's a story fpr another day) i think they've just found a niche market with the powdery sugar scents that are trending atm and didnt really put much thought or feeling into it at all.
But the original really is something special and i really hope with its re release; it will urge other fragrance houses to go back to their roots and bring out more classic scents, rather than all the patchouli/ praline combos and fruity sugar bombs that are in our faces lately.

It starts out with a bang..this could easily put someone off...it's quite a jumble of strong citrus notes and basil. It smells like an extremely expensive soap. If you are not a fan of soapy, still give it a chance because it reveals a lot more.. The aldehydes are prominent and give it a glamourous sparkle. This one REALLY needs to settle and warm up before it's true beauty is revealed (as i said)

After a while all the notes mesh and waft in a way that still makes me swoon..even after smelling it so many times on different people and myself. I just cannot get enough of it. It's powdery (as i said) but..ultra classy and feminine at the same time. Not baby powder.... sexy powder! It's extremely difficult to describe for me, I just know its a masterpeice.

Now I hear D&G are discontinuing it...booooo! I have ran out and bought myself 300mls of this to make sure I'll never be without it and am considering a fourth 100ml. (edit..I'm now on my fifth, I need to go on "hoarders"

This scent needs to be tried and used carefully to get the real feel of it. It's an absolute delight to wear and is a huge statement. Too much will knock people out....I'm only just becoming brave enough to wear it myself after all these years.

Oh Red Cap...you are breathtakingly beautiful...there is no other like you.

THIS IS PERFUME PERFECTION!

Mortazuma 12/06/13 10:34

There comes a time in a girl's life when she realizes she doesn't need to fit in with the rest of her all flowers-and-candy spritzed peers and becomes her own unique person.

This perfume, is not for just -any- woman. If it didn't "work out" for someone, it was for good reason. It just wasn't meant for YOU, darlings.

When I worked in a perfumeria, this was a rather tough sell since it was deemed somewhat overpowering and not a very "feminine" scent. My body chemistry begs to differ. By "feminine" I've learned what they really meant...they meant "girly" and this is not a girly scent. Its too sophisticated for that and I shall explain.

Within minutes of wear, it feels like exotic spicy flowers took residence within your pores and bloomed from your body heat. The magic lies in the drydown though, where the complexity of this perfume reveals what secrets lies beneath the skin. It seems to conjure up that silent yet smoldering lady that can seduce with merely a cocked brow. Silent, yes...but by no means timid.

If I were asked, what kind of woman comes to mind when I smell this...I would say it is for a woman who doesn't have to try hard or even at all to obtain attention, she exudes a raw feminine sensuality without much effort, she is comfortable in her own skin without needing anyone else's opinions, she is someone silent and observant but intriguing, she'd be a woman few would know intimately but several would find hard to forget...a tigress, pretty much.

This is why I say that this fragrance isn't for everyone. It simply wasn't meant for that and the intention can be smelled a smile away ;)



P.S. I am saddened that this fragrance may be joining the Glorious Perfumes Graveyard. I do hope they relaunch them in some years. It would be a terrible shame to lose this unique and erotic fragrance as a thing of the past.

violetelle 02/20/22 15:36

For me, this fragrance is the epitome of glamour. I want to share with you the story of my parents’ friend Brigitte…

Brigitte is French. She smokes long cigarettes, drinks wine and hosts fabulous but laid back parties. She has olive skin, short dyed caramel hair and wears gold jewellery. She’s unashamedly herself. She has a sultry low voice and laughs loudly and unreservedly. She’s fiercely loyal. Nails always done. She rides motorbikes. She wears D&G red cap.

I know this doesn’t tell you much about the fragrance itself but all the notes are listed here anyway. I remember it as very soapy but that description really doesn’t do it justice. It’s soapy in a refined, pure and very expensive way.

You might expect someone like Brigitte to wear a smoky, oriental scent. But she didn’t need it. She smoked Marlboros and wore high quality leather. She was also a mother and wife who was always well turned out and impeccably stylish. This scent just suited her perfectly.

Brigitte moved back to France, and I haven’t seen her in years. But she left an impression on me. She became my reference point for glamour at such a young age, before I even knew what glamour was.

In sum, this fragrance is classy, sophisticated and timeless - much like Brigitte!!

EllieJP 08/30/25 03:49

I have Italian-made bottles. Around 1992, during Japan’s bubble economy, these perfumes were widely available, so they’re relatively easy to find here！

They have a rare scent that brings back memories of the 1990s. On my skin, the aldehydes lingered longer than expected, revealing the floral notes not in an hour, but after about three hours. Honestly, I was surprised by that initial sparkling “bang” of fragrance. I recommend it when you want to immerse yourself in the 1990s vibe. I happen to have quite a few, so I’m planning to part with two Italian-made bottles.

*Telling Italian-made bottles apart is quite simple. The red cap is semi-transparent, not completely clear, and if you look closely, the bottom of the bottle forms a beautiful arch. Bottles made outside Italy do not have this elegant arched bottom. It’s impressive how much attention to detail goes into these subtle features.
